interactionPlan.concept: The phase component of an image's Fourier Transform carries the structural and edge information, while the amplitude component carries frequency intensity and style information.
learningObjectives: After engaging with this figure, the student will understand that the spatial location of edges and shapes in an image is encoded primarily within the phase of its Fourier transform.
The student will be able to explain why swapping the amplitude and phase of two images results in reconstructed images that retain the structural identity of their phase sources.
The student will understand how the amplitude component influences the overall color distribution and contrast style of the reconstructed image without altering its fundamental geometry.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: Structure lives in the phase, while style lives in the amplitude: if you swap them, you change the 'texture' but keep the 'shape' of the phase contributor.

interactions.label: Structure (Phase)
interactions.effect: Switches the phase component of the reconstructed image between the Sailboat and the Stop Sign, instantly flipping the recognizable subject matter of the output.
interactions.teaches: Demonstrates that the phase component exclusively determines which object (Sailboat or Stop Sign) is structurally perceived in the image.

interactions.label: Style (Amplitude)
interactions.effect: Smoothly interpolates the amplitude component of the Fourier transform from 100% Sailboat to 100% Stop Sign, changing the overall color cast, texture, and intensity distribution of the output.
interactions.teaches: Shows how the amplitude component acts like a global frequency and color filter, transforming the texture and luminance style without shifting the structural boundaries determined by the phase.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: The layout consists of a two-row pipeline. The left column shows two input images: a sailboat on water (top) and a red octagonal stop sign (bottom). The middle columns display their respective Fourier Transform components (2D phase maps showing noise-like details, and 2D amplitude spectrums showing star-like central frequency spikes). The right column shows the reconstructed crossover images. Visual interactive links (arrows) should dynamically adjust opacity or highlight paths as the user slides the controls, showing which source's phase and amplitude are combining to form the active output image.
